topic: Why does a week have 7 days?
title: Why Does a Week Have 7 Days?
description: No planet spins in 7 days, yet the whole world uses a 7-day week. The answer is written in the ancient night sky.
sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Calendar - The seven-day week

scenes.label: Thousands of years ago
scenes.narration: Thousands of years ago, a farmer stared at the night sky and noticed the Moon was changing shape.

scenes.question: Why does a week have 7 days?
scenes.narration: So why does every week, everywhere, have exactly seven days?
Meet Tiko. He needs to know when to plant, when to trade and when to rest. But there are no calendars.
So he watches the Moon. New, half, full, half again. Each change takes about seven days.

scenes.label: 7 moving lights
scenes.narration: Then he notices seven bright lights that wander across the sky: the Sun, the Moon and five planets.
But every town counts days its own way. Market day here is rest day there. Trading turns into chaos.
The seven-day idea wins. It spreads from Babylon, through Jewish tradition, all the way to Rome.

scenes.label: Sun-day, Moon-day
scenes.narration: That's why we still say Sunday and Monday: the Sun's day and the Moon's day.
So every week is a tiny map of the ancient sky. Follow for more stories of how things began.
